one_paragraph_summary: Panganiban delivers the doctrinal anchor for Grace Poe's presidential eligibility on residency. The Constitution states no person may be elected President (or Vice President) unless he is 'a resident of the Philippines for at least 10 years immediately preceding such election.' In election law, 'residence' is equated with 'domicile,' not necessarily a home address -- a man may have several residences but only one domicile. There are three kinds: domicile of origin (a child follows the parents'), domicile by operation of law, and domicile of choice (freely made by a person of legal age), which 'imports not only the intention to reside in one fixed place but also personal presence in that place, coupled with conduct indicative of such intention.' Three settled rules govern: everyone must always have one domicile; once established, it remains until a new one is acquired; a person can have only one domicile at any given time. Applied to Poe: as a foundling found in Jaro, Iloilo, she acquired the domicile (and citizenship) of her parents who are presumed Filipinos -- so her domicile of origin is Jaro, Iloilo. After she married an American and moved to the US, she lost her domicile of origin and followed her husband's domicile in America. When she and her husband moved back permanently after FPJ's death, she acquired a new domicile of choice. Settled jurisprudence confirms: in Marcos v. Comelec (Sept 18, 1995), the Court held that the fact of residence -- not a COC statement -- is decisive; Imelda's honest mistake of writing 'seven months' for a congressional seat did not foreclose her; similarly, Poe's honest mistake of writing 'six years and six months' in her Senate COC is not binding proof. Cordora v. Comelec (Feb 19, 2009) held that even foreigners may establish Philippine domicile; Japson v. Comelec (Jan 19, 2009) ruled that a former Filipino naturalized abroad may re-establish domicile here even before reacquisition of citizenship; Jalosjos v. Comelec (Oct 19, 2010) held that abandonment of an Australian home, renunciation of Australian citizenship, and settling in Zamboanga Sibugay show 'intent to change domicile for good'; Maquiling v. Comelec (April 16, 2013) clarified that using an American passport after renouncing American citizenship effectively reverses the renunciation. Poe's intent to acquire a new domicile of choice (animus manendi) is proven by her return to the Philippines in the first half of 2005, enrollment of her children here in June 2005, property purchase in late 2005, and construction of her QC family home in early 2006. Her intent to abandon her old domicile (animus non revertendi) is shown by the delisting of her children from their American schools in May 2005 and the sale of her California home in April 2006. Her physical presence is evidenced by passport entries and other authentic documents. Based on these acts, facts, laws and jurisprudence -- unless belied by contravening facts unknown to CJP -- Senator Poe will surpass the 10-year residency requirement come Election Day, May 9, 2016. In a postscript, CJP congratulates Dean Raul Pangalangan for his ICC election, noting he tried for over 10 years to help him land a Supreme Court seat -- 'But the Lord did not will it. Now I know why. Because he was meant for something bigger, loftier and better-suited to his unique specialization.'
